system:
You are the Mediator on a ten-member emergency triage panel. You pinpoint exactly where the panel disagrees and which single fact or ESI step would settle it. Your trait shapes HOW you reason, never which direction you lean. Do not shift toward a more or less urgent level because of your trait; follow the ESI reference below.

ESI v4 (1 = most urgent). Apply A-D in order; stop at the first that fits.
A. Needs immediate life-saving intervention? -> ESI 1. (Unresponsive, apneic/pulseless, severe
   respiratory distress, SpO2 < 90%, shock, unstable major trauma, overdose with poor breathing.)
B. Should not wait? -> ESI 2 if high-risk situation (e.g. possible ACS, stroke, ectopic, suicidal or
   homicidal, high-risk mechanism, febrile infant, immunocompromised with fever), OR new
   confusion/lethargy/disorientation, OR severe pain/distress (>= 7/10).
C. Count distinct resource types: labs, ECG, X-ray, CT/MRI/US, IV fluids, IV/IM/nebulized meds,
   specialty consult, simple procedure (1), complex procedure (2). Not resources: exam, POC tests,
   saline lock, oral meds, tetanus, refill, simple wound care, splint/sling/crutches.
   0 -> ESI 5; 1 -> ESI 4; 2+ -> go to D.
D. Danger-zone vitals -> consider ESI 2, else ESI 3. HR/RR limits: <3 mo >180/>50; 3 mo-3 y
   >160/>40; 3-8 y >140/>30; >8 y >100/>20. Any age SpO2 < 92%. Fever >= 38.0 C: age 1-28 days
   is at least ESI 2; 1-3 months consider ESI 2.

Use only clinical information from the vignette. Reply with JSON only:
{"esi": 1-5, "confidence": 0.0-1.0, "key_findings": [<=3 phrases, <10 words each], "rationale": "<=60 words"}

PATIENT VIGNETTE
A 16-year-old male wearing a swimsuit walks into the ED. He explains that he dove into a pool, and his face struck the bottom. You notice an abrasion on his forehead and nose as he tells you that he needs to see a doctor because of tingling in both hands.

Assign the ESI level.
text: {"esi": 3, "confidence": 0.95, "key_findings": ["Teenager after facial trauma", "Tingling in both hands"], "rationale": "The patient is a teenager who suffered facial trauma from a dive into a pool, reporting tingling in both hands. This suggests potential neurological involvement, warranting further evaluation. The injury does not meet ESI 1 criteria (immediate life-saving intervention) nor ESI 2 criteria (high-risk situations or severe pain/distress) based on the current information. There are no distinct resource types mentioned, and danger-zone vitals aren't indicated. The combination of these factors leads to an ESI level of 3."}
